subject.title: [Bug] Session flush blocks write tool completely during compaction

question: Should memory-triggered compaction runs be allowed to write unrelated workspace files, and if so under which normalized path and sandbox boundary?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes a silent housekeeping turn from one append-only target to broader workspace write authority, which is a security and product-policy choice.

options.title: Approve a narrow exception contract
options.body: Allow non-memory workspace writes to pass through the existing write tool's workspace and sandbox checks while keeping memory-path writes restricted to the configured append-only target, with focused regression tests and docs.

options.title: Keep the hard single-target guard
options.body: Preserve the current safety boundary and document that memory flush may block unrelated writes until the flush cycle ends or memory flush is disabled.

options.title: Add an explicit operator opt-in
options.body: Introduce a config-gated broader write mode with upgrade docs, but accept the added configuration surface and compatibility burden.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow exception contract
recommendation.body: Allow non-memory workspace writes to pass through the existing write tool's workspace and sandbox checks while keeping memory-path writes restricted to the configured append-only target, with focused regression tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision balances the original pre-compaction memory-flush product behavior against the project's security-default posture.
